display.title: After Purim: Why the Megillah Calls Us Yehudim
display.summary_short: A week after Purim, Uncle Yossi explains why the Megillah calls the Jewish people Yehudim: we thank Hashem and acknowledge Him alone, just as Mordechai did.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given one week after Purim. Uncle Yossi teaches that every Yom Tov is not only a memory of the past but a lesson for today, and asks what message should stay with us from Purim. Throughout the Torah we are usually called B'nai Yisrael, the children of Yaakov Avinu, but in the Megillah we are called Yehudim. The Sages connect the name Yehudi to the word 'modeh', which means both to thank, as in Modeh Ani each morning, and to admit, as in Modim in Shemoneh Esrei, where we acknowledge that Hashem is the one and only G-d. The Sages also teach that whoever rejects idol worship is called a Yehudi, and Mordechai HaYehudi set the example for all generations by refusing to bow or even stir before Haman. Uncle Yossi encourages children to stay proud Yehudim all year, trusting in Hashem as the G-d of miracles, and closes with a prayer to see the greatest miracle of all: Hashem's return to Tzion with the coming of Moshiach.
display.lesson: We are called Yehudim because we thank Hashem and acknowledge Him alone; stay proud of that name all year long.
